newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest power rises on cold weather, natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest power rises on cold weather, natgas.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Midwest were sharply higher Monday on the heels of stronger natural gas prices and cold weather forecasts, industry sources said.

Temperatures throughout most of the Midwest are expected to be much below normal through at least early next week, falling about 20-30 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal Wednesday through Friday in the southern plains.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery were pegged at $28.00-28.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), up from Friday's range of $21.50-23.50, market sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were assessed around $14.00, as compared with Friday's $12.00-14.00 trading range.

In MAIN, peak, non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery were steady to higher in the $25.00-27.00 range, with late deals reported done as high as $28.00. These prices compare with Friday's $23.00-26.00 trading range.
For the remainder of the week, peak prices in MAIN were at a premium to next-day around $30.00, traders said.
MAIN off peak power was talked in the $14.00-15.00 range, up from Friday's $12.00-14.00 trading range.
Hourly power prices in MAIN were talked in the low-$30s.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Tuesday were higher at $23.00-26.00.
For the remainder of the week, ECAR peak prices were talked in the $28.00-30.00 per MWh range.
January/February ECAR prices were in the $25.25-25.50 area, traders said, while the March market hovered around $21.25-22.00.
Off-peak, non-firm next-day ECAR power was also higher in the $15.00-16.00 range, up from Friday's trading range at $11.00-14.00.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak non-firm power for Tuesday was quoted mostly in the $25.00-26.00 range, as compared with Friday's $21.00-23.00 trading range.
Southern SPP prices were talked in the low-$30s.
January/February peak prices in SPP were talked in the $28.25-28.50 range, up from Friday's $26.75-27.50 range.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were notionally higher around $15.00, as compared with Friday's trading range of $12.00-14.00.
Separately, Entergy's 858 megawatt (MW) Arkansas 2 nuclear unit is expected to return to the grid Tuesday after shutting November 16 for repairs.
Also Northern States Power Co's 222 MW Riverside 8 coal unit in Minneapolis, Minn., shut Friday, will likely restart later today.
MidAmerican Energy Co said its 300 MW Neal 2 coal unit near Sioux City, Iowa, shut Saturday due to a boiler tube leak, is expected to restart sometime Tuesday.
--H McCulloch, New York Power Desk +212-859-1628
